answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake before it can place orders or earn trust. When an agent is caught double-spending or coordinating fake trades, the protocol slashes that stake and limits the value of its next transactions. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital in every persona, not merely mint names; karst, timber, and cedar can label distinct markets, but none makes duplicated identities free.
